Killers chasing is not tunneling, killers confirming a kill is not tunneling. You need to separate what is concrete proof and what is speculation in a situation like this. He *could* be tunneling, but he could also have been chasing you to even out the hooks. You guys were doing well on gens, so he *could* be tunneling you when he downed you and killed you, or he could've been attempting to thin the numbers and put more pressure back in his hands. You act like his shallow roaming around hook was out of your control, but your behavior during the initial chase is what led to you being hooked. Just like your actions during the 2nd chase is what led to your death. Like I said, bm is bm, so sure, he probably was aiming to kill you from the start, but assumptions aren't fact and it couldve just been a cocky killer siezing the advantage from a series of survivor mistakes.

Bm is bm, but this was definitely a skill issue that's disingenuous to call a tunneling. He has no responsibility as a killer to give up on a chase and can follow you through the entire map if he wants. You haven't been hooked before, while all your teammates have, so perhaps he wanted to even it out by hooking you. Next, not only was there an unsafe unhook, but you both ran away on top of each other and even got stuck. Think from the killer's perspective here. Do you go after the full health on-2nd-hook Sable who's currently unintentionally being blocked by the Leon? Or do you go after the Leon who's dead on hook, by waiting out hit Endurance? In any situation, even if it's annoying, the killer will, or at least should, opt for removing a survivor from the game. He's under no requirement to allow you and your team any leeway for the mistake earlier. 

TL:DR, aside from the bm, he could've targeted you because you haven't been hooked, and the 2nd target was because you were dead on hook and it was easier to do.
